articles.title: Maceió tem o metro quadrado mais caro do Nordeste; veja ranking | G1
articles.standfirst: Preço médio dos imóveis residenciais na capital alagoana chegou a R$ 9.974 por metro quadrado em agosto. Bairro da Pajuçara lidera ranking.
articles.summary: Preço médio dos imóveis residenciais na capital alagoana chegou a R$ 9.974 por metro quadrado em agosto. Bairro da Pajuçara lidera ranking.
articles.body:
Orla de Maceió panorâmica — Foto: Kaio Fragoso

Maceió tem o metro quadrado mais caro entre as capitais do Nordeste, segundo o Índice FipeZap de Venda Residencial referente a agosto de 2026. O preço médio dos imóveis residenciais anunciados na capital alagoana chegou a R$ 9.974 por metro quadrado .

🔎O Índice FipeZap acompanha a variação dos preços de imóveis residenciais a partir de anúncios publicados na internet. O levantamento monitora 56 cidades brasileiras e é desenvolvido pela Fundação Instituto de Pesquisas Econômicas (Fipe) em parceria com o Grupo OLX.

O valor coloca Maceió à frente de Fortaleza , segunda colocada na região, com R$ 9.502/m², e do Recife , com R$ 8.912/m². Entre as 22 capitais brasileiras monitoradas pelo levantamento, Maceió tem o 8º maior preço médio.

Veja o preço médio do metro quadrado nas capitais do Nordeste:

Apesar de apresentar o maior preço médio da região, Maceió teve a menor valorização entre as capitais nordestinas em 2026. De janeiro a agosto, os preços anunciados na cidade subiram 3,54%.

No acumulado dos últimos 12 meses, a alta foi de 5,50%, também o menor percentual entre as capitais do Nordeste monitoradas pelo índice. Ainda assim, a valorização ficou acima da inflação usada como referência pelo levantamento no período, de 4,14%.

Em agosto, os preços em Maceió subiram 0,12%, após queda de 0,04% registrada em julho.

Entre os bairros e áreas mais representativos considerados pelo FipeZap em Maceió, a Pajuçara apresentou o maior preço médio em agosto, de R$ 13.933/m². Na sequência, aparecem Ponta Verde, Jacarecica, Jatiúca e Cruz das Almas.

Entre essas áreas, a Serraria teve a maior valorização nos últimos 12 meses, de 23,5%. Já a Pajuçara apresentou queda de 0,6% no período.

O relatório ressalta que os valores representam preços anunciados de imóveis residenciais, e não necessariamente os preços pelos quais os imóveis foram efetivamente vendidos.

Mulheres que desejam colocar o dispositivo intrauterino (DIU) gratuitamente pelo Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS) podem procurar uma das 23 unidades de saúde de Maceió habilitadas para realizar o procedimento.

O atendimento começa na Atenção Primária. A usuária passa por uma avaliação e recebe orientações sobre como o DIU funciona, indicações, benefícios e possíveis efeitos adversos.

Antes da inserção, a equipe de saúde verifica as condições do útero, descarta uma possível gravidez e avalia a existência de infecções. Segundo a coordenadora da Saúde da Mulher de Maceió, Suzângela Mendonça, o acompanhamento continua depois da colocação.

“Após o procedimento, a paciente continua sendo acompanhada e, em cerca de duas semanas, realiza ultrassonografia para confirmar o posicionamento correto do dispositivo”, explicou a coordenadora.

O primeiro passo é procurar uma das unidades que oferecem o procedimento. Durante o atendimento, a equipe vai avaliar se a paciente pode utilizar o método e solicitar os exames necessários.

articles.title: Casa da Mulher oferece assistência a vítimas de violência em Alfenas | G1
articles.standfirst: Equipamento reúne atendimento jurídico, social e psicológico em um único local, sem exigir boletim de ocorrência ou medida protetiva para o primeiro acolhimento.
articles.summary: Equipamento reúne atendimento jurídico, social e psicológico em um único local, sem exigir boletim de ocorrência ou medida protetiva para o primeiro acolhimento.
articles.body:
A cidade de Alfenas passou a contar com a Casa da Mulher, espaço criado para oferecer assistência jurídica, social e psicológica a vítimas de violência doméstica em um único local. O objetivo é ampliar o acolhimento e ajudar a absorver o aumento dos pedidos de medidas protetivas registrados no município.

Além dos atendimentos, o espaço conta com uma sala específica para o público LGBTQIA+ e abrigará um observatório de dados sobre a violência. A secretária de Políticas Públicas para Mulheres, Kátia Goiatá, destacou que a unidade foi criada para atender uma demanda crescente na cidade.

“A Casa da Mulher surge com essa necessidade de atender a esse tipo de demanda. As mulheres tanto podem chegar até a Casa da Mulher de maneira espontânea ou encaminhada por outros equipamentos que já existem na nossa cidade de Alfenas”, afirmou.

Casa da Mulher é inaugurada para oferecer assistência jurídica, social e psicológica a vítimas de violência em Alfena — Foto: Reprodução EPTV

Segundo a secretária, não é necessário apresentar boletim de ocorrência ou medida protetiva para buscar atendimento no local. Ela explicou que a assistência jurídica oferecida pela unidade pode auxiliar as vítimas em todas as etapas do processo.

“Necessariamente, elas não precisam chegar aqui com isso, porque, inclusive, a nossa advogada, que vai prestar assistência jurídica, pode ajudar nesse sentido, até acompanhar essa mulher vítima de violência ao próprio batalhão, para fazer o boletim de ocorrência, ou à própria DEAM, Delegacia da Mulher”, disse.

Kátia Goiatá afirmou que a criação da Casa da Mulher vinha sendo planejada há cerca de dois anos pela Secretaria de Políticas Públicas para Mulheres.

“Esse espaço viabiliza um atendimento mais rápido, mais célere para essas mulheres, mais humanizado, com acolhimento, com um olhar de acolhimento e não de julgamento e muito menos de condenação. Então, isso, a gente estava há um tempo já com esse desejo de abrir as portas e a gente conseguiu”, ressaltou.

A secretária também destacou a criação de uma sala voltada ao público LGBTQIA+, especialmente para mulheres trans.

“Exatamente. A gente sabe que essas mulheres trans, elas são invisíveis. Então, aqui o nosso trabalho com esse atendimento, a gente vai atrás, inclusive com o observatório que a gente também criou, justamente para, através desses dados, a gente poder ter a condição de fazer uma política pública eficiente e sem desperdício de dinheiro público”, afirmou.

Apesar do acolhimento oferecido, a Casa da Mulher não funciona como abrigo para vítimas. A proposta é centralizar serviços de atendimento, orientação e acompanhamento em um mesmo espaço.

articles.summary: Segundo a concessionária, os serviços devem começar entre 20h e 20h30. A previsão é que os trabalhos sejam concluídos por volta das 10h de domingo (6).
articles.body:
Teresina terá interrupção no abastecimento de água — Foto: g1 Piauí

Mais de 140 bairros e localidades de Teresina ficarão temporariamente sem abastecimento de água entre a noite deste sábado (5) e o meio-dia de domingo (6). Segundo a concessionária, os serviços devem começar entre 20h e 20h30.

A previsão é que os trabalhos sejam concluídos por volta das 10h de domingo (6). Em seguida, o abastecimento será retomado gradualmente, com normalização prevista até as 12h.

Segundo a Águas de Teresina, a interrupção foi programada para a realização de serviços de manutenção e melhorias na rede de distribuição, com o objetivo de reforçar o sistema para os meses mais quentes do ano, quando a demanda por água costuma aumentar.

A manutenção integra a Operação B-R-O-BRÓ, realizada para reforçar o sistema de abastecimento durante os meses mais quentes do ano. Para a execução dos serviços, a Estação de Tratamento de Água Sul (ETA Sul) será desligada temporariamente.

Mais de 80 profissionais atuarão em sete frentes de trabalho simultâneas na estação e na rede de distribuição. As equipes farão a otimização de equipamentos, a limpeza de filtros, a substituição de trechos de tubulação e a limpeza da rede em mais de 30 pontos da cidade.

A concessionária também instalará três novos registros nos bairros Saci, Três Andares e Vila da Paz. Segundo a empresa, os equipamentos permitirão isolar áreas menores durante futuras manutenções, reduzindo o impacto no abastecimento.

A Águas de Teresina orienta os moradores das regiões afetadas a armazenarem água com antecedência para atividades essenciais e evitarem desperdícios durante o período da interrupção. Imóveis com caixa-d'água dimensionada adequadamente devem sofrer menos impacto.

Em caso de dúvidas ou solicitações emergenciais, os clientes podem entrar em contato com a concessionária pelo telefone e WhatsApp 0800 223 2000, disponível 24 horas por dia. O atendimento também pode ser feito pelo aplicativo Águas App.

articles.title: Incêndio Viver Melhor III: DPE aciona Justiça por auxílio-moradia | G1
articles.standfirst: Incêndio aconteceu no dia 9 de agosto, no bloco 5 do residencial, no bairro Monte das Oliveiras. Um cachorro morreu durante o incêndio e moradores relataram que um bebê foi resgatado pela janela.
articles.summary: A Defensoria Pública do Amazonas pede auxílio-moradia para 16 famílias e laudo técnico sobre a estrutura do Residencial Viver Melhor III após o incêndio de agosto.
articles.body:
Incêndio atinge prédio residencial em Manaus — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

A Defensoria Pública do Amazonas (DPE-AM) acionou a Justiça para garantir auxílio-moradia a 16 famílias afetadas pelo incêndio que atingiu um bloco do Residencial Viver Melhor III, na Zona Norte de Manaus . O órgão também pediu uma avaliação técnica completa da estrutura do prédio antes que os moradores possam voltar aos apartamentos .

O incêndio aconteceu no dia 9 de agosto, no bloco 5 do residencial, no bairro Monte das Oliveiras. O fogo começou em um apartamento no térreo e também atingiu o imóvel vizinho. Um cachorro morreu durante o incêndio e moradores relataram que um bebê foi resgatado pela janela .

Segundo a Defensoria, quase um mês após o incêndio, parte das famílias ainda não recebeu auxílio para deixar o local . Das 16 famílias atingidas, cinco já receberam algum tipo de suporte, enquanto as demais aguardam medidas emergenciais.

Na ação, a Defensoria pediu que o Estado, a Prefeitura de Manaus e o Instituto Municipal de Planejamento Urbano (Implurb) apresentem, em até 72 horas, um laudo técnico sobre as condições de segurança do bloco.

A avaliação deverá incluir a estrutura do prédio, as instalações elétricas e os sistemas de prevenção e combate a incêndios.

O órgão também pediu que Estado e Município garantam auxílio-moradia emergencial às 16 famílias e mantenham o benefício para os moradores que já começaram a recebê-lo.

Relatórios da Defesa Civil do Estado e da Defesa Civil de Manaus apontaram problemas na estrutura do bloco atingido . Entre eles estão fissuras, desagregação e deterioração superficial da laje de concreto .

Os dois órgãos recomendaram uma avaliação estrutural completa, feita por um profissional habilitado, principalmente nas lajes, vigas e pilares que podem ter sido afetados pelo calor das chamas.

Por isso, segundo a Defensoria, ainda não é possível liberar de forma definitiva o retorno dos moradores aos apartamentos.

"A situação das famílias é dramática, porque já se passou quase um mês desde a ocorrência do incêndio e nenhuma resposta efetiva sobre o futuro foi dada a elas. A grande questão é se esse prédio ficará de pé. Os relatórios da Defesa Civil do Estado e do Município também apontam para essa mesma dúvida. É isso que estamos demandando com essa providência judicial", afirmou o defensor público Carlos Almeida, titular da Defensoria Pública Especializada em Interesses Coletivos (DPEIC).

Os moradores procuraram a Defensoria logo após o incêndio. No dia 12 de agosto, uma equipe da instituição esteve no residencial acompanhada de um profissional de Engenharia.

Durante a vistoria, foi constatado que o fogo teria atingido a caixa de energia do prédio, localizada no térreo, o que poderia representar risco de novos incêndios.

Depois disso, a Defensoria reuniu órgãos municipais e estaduais responsáveis por habitação, assistência social e Defesa Civil, além das concessionárias Âmbar Energia Amazonas S.A. e Águas de Manaus.

O encontro discutiu medidas para atender as famílias, os reparos necessários no prédio e possíveis responsabilidades pelos problemas.

Os órgãos envolvidos tinham até 21 de agosto para apresentar soluções. Segundo a Defensoria, o prazo terminou sem que as medidas consideradas necessárias fossem adotadas. Por isso, o caso foi levado à Justiça.

O incêndio aconteceu na tarde de 9 de agosto, em um apartamento no térreo do bloco 5 do Viver Melhor III, na Rua das Cachoeiras, no bairro Monte das Oliveiras.

Segundo moradores, o imóvel onde o fogo começou funcionava como uma oficina eletrônica e tinha madeira e líquidos inflamáveis. O proprietário informou que não estava em casa no momento do incêndio e não quis falar com a reportagem.

Moradores ajudaram a retirar pessoas dos apartamentos. Algumas foram retiradas pelas janelas com auxílio de escadas externas.

Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros Militar do Amazonas (CBMAM), 24 militares e oito viaturas foram mobilizados para combater o fogo. Foram usados cerca de 12 mil litros de água na ocorrência.

Um cachorro que estava no imóvel onde o incêndio começou morreu.

Bebê é retirado pela janela durante incêndio em prédio na Zona Norte de Manaus. — Foto: Foto: Arquivo Pessoal

Um bebê de aproximadamente dois meses foi retirado pela janela por moradores durante o incêndio.

Segundo testemunhas, a mãe da criança cortou os pés durante a fuga. O bebê foi levado inicialmente para uma casa próxima e, depois, encaminhado pelo Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu).

Outras duas crianças que estavam no quarto andar também foram resgatadas pelo Corpo de Bombeiros.

Na ocasião, a Secretaria de Estado de Saúde do Amazonas (SES-AM) informou que 18 pessoas deram entrada em unidades da rede estadual de saúde após o incêndio. Todas receberam atendimento e tiveram alta no mesmo dia do sinistro.

articles.title: Sem frutos suficientes, macacos-prego mudam o cardápio e caçam mais | G1
articles.standfirst: Pesquisa acompanhou animais por 45 meses no Piauí e registrou 446 episódios de consumo de vertebrados, entre lagartos, roedores, aves, serpentes e gambás.
articles.summary: Pesquisa acompanhou animais por 45 meses no Piauí e registrou 446 episódios de consumo de vertebrados, entre lagartos, roedores, aves, serpentes e gambás.
articles.body:
Macaco-Prego-Amarelo (Sapajus libidinosus) — Foto: naativa / iNaturalist

Frutas, folhas, flores e insetos fazem parte do cardápio dos macacos-prego, mas, quando a disponibilidade de frutos diminui, pequenos vertebrados podem ganhar espaço na alimentação . Um estudo publicado na revista científica PLOS One mostrou que esses primatas aumentam a predação de animais como lagartos, roedores, aves, serpentes e marsupiais em períodos de menor oferta de frutos.

A pesquisa acompanhou dois grupos de macacos-prego ( Sapajus libidinosus ) na Fazenda Boa Vista, no Piauí, por 45 meses. Segundo os autores, trata-se do registro mais extenso já realizado sobre a predação de vertebrados por essa espécie .

Ao todo, foram 5.093 horas de observação e 446 eventos de consumo de vertebrados. A taxa média registrada foi de 6,34 episódios de predação a cada 100 horas de acompanhamento.

Os animais consumiram principalmente pequenos vertebrados. Entre os 281 episódios utilizados em uma das análises do estudo, foram registrados 123 lagartos, 80 roedores, 34 aves — incluindo ovos e filhotes —, 15 marsupiais, 12 serpentes, dois morcegos e uma iguana. Outras 14 presas não puderam ser identificadas.

Segundo os pesquisadores, o consumo de vertebrados foi observado em machos e fêmeas e também em diferentes faixas etárias. O estudo considera esse comportamento habitual nos grupos acompanhados.

Veja mais notícias do Terra da Gente, no g1:

Um dos principais resultados foi a relação entre a disponibilidade de frutos e a frequência da predação.

Os dados mostraram uma associação negativa significativa: quanto menor a disponibilidade de frutos, maior a taxa de consumo de vertebrados . Já a quantidade de insetos disponível no ambiente não apresentou associação estatisticamente significativa com a taxa geral de predação.

Conforme os autores do artigo, os resultados identificaram os pequenos vertebrados como uma importante fonte de energia para os macacos-prego quando há redução na disponibilidade de frutos.

Ao Jornal da USP, a pesquisadora Patrícia Izar, professora do Instituto de Psicologia da Universidade de São Paulo e uma das autoras do trabalho, explicou que os macacos-prego não têm uma alimentação especializada.

“Eles comem frutos, folhas, flores, invertebrados e vertebrados”, afirmou. Segundo a pesquisadora, os pequenos animais funcionam como fonte de proteína e gordura e podem complementar a dieta quando outros recursos ficam menos acessíveis.

Na Fazenda Boa Vista, os frutos de palmeiras ajudam a explicar parte dessa dinâmica. De acordo com Patrícia, os cocos são abundantes durante a estação seca, mas diminuem entre dezembro e fevereiro, durante o período chuvoso. Nessa época, o consumo de vertebrados aumenta.

Os próprios autores fazem uma ressalva no artigo: a relação observada pode ser fortemente influenciada pelas variações na disponibilidade desses frutos de palmeiras, ricos em lipídios e proteínas.

Pesquisa revela quando macacos-prego passam a consumir mais animais — Foto: leinawander / iNaturalist

O estudo também detalhou quais partes das presas eram consumidas.

As aves geralmente eram ingeridas inteiras. Quando isso não ocorria, os macacos costumavam consumir cérebro e vísceras. Entre os mamíferos, cauda e patas estavam entre as partes frequentemente ingeridas e, em alguns episódios, também os olhos.

Lagartos e lagartixas podiam ter pés, cauda, olhos, cérebro, pele e vísceras consumidos. Já nas serpentes, os pesquisadores observaram que os animais frequentemente descartavam a cabeça e ingeriam o restante do corpo, principalmente os órgãos internos. No período acompanhado, apenas machos foram vistos consumindo cobras.

Macaco-prego. — Foto: Tiago Falótico/Creative Commons

Segundo Patrícia Izar, em divulgação da USP, uma possível explicação para a preferência inicial pelo cérebro está no conteúdo energético desse tecido.

“O cérebro é rico em lipídio, então, é uma fonte importante de energia”, explicou.

O artigo registra ainda que cérebro e vísceras, por serem partes mais macias, eram consumidos mais rapidamente do que músculos e outros tecidos.

Machos apresentaram maior taxa de predação

As diferenças também apareceram entre os próprios macacos.

Os machos apresentaram uma taxa estimada de consumo de vertebrados 1,4 vez maior que a das fêmeas. Filhotes consumiram vertebrados a aproximadamente um quinto da taxa observada em adultos, enquanto os juvenis não apresentaram diferença estatisticamente significativa em relação aos adultos.

Patrícia explicou que diferenças de tamanho corporal e necessidade energética estão entre as hipóteses para o maior índice entre machos, mas ressaltou que ainda faltam estudos capazes de determinar a causa.

“Temos essas hipóteses, mas a gente precisa de muito mais trabalhos para conseguir responder a essas perguntas”, afirmou.

Outro resultado reforçou a ligação entre disponibilidade de alimento e predação. Um dos grupos estudados recebia diariamente uma oferta suplementar de alimentos, enquanto o outro não. A taxa estimada de predação no grupo sem suplementação foi 1,88 vez maior.

Apesar da variedade de presas, a maior parte do consumo registrado esteve associada a eventos individuais.

Nos episódios classificados pelos pesquisadores, 82,14% ocorreram de forma individual, contra 17,86% envolvendo mais de um animal. Em parte desses episódios coletivos, houve transferência de carne ou de outras partes da carcaça entre os macacos.

“Quando o animal é caçado, os outros macacos tentam pegar pedacinhos”, contou Patrícia, explicando que outros indivíduos podem se aproximar depois que uma presa é capturada.

Macacos-prego trocam parte dos frutos por presas animais em períodos de escassez — Foto: leandrorezende / iNaturalist

O trabalho também usa os macacos-prego como modelo comparativo para investigar uma questão mais ampla: como o consumo de animais pode ter participado da evolução do comportamento predatório humano.

Os autores destacam que seres humanos são os únicos primatas atuais conhecidos por explorar regularmente animais de tamanho semelhante ou maior que o próprio corpo. Antes do surgimento desse padrão, pequenos vertebrados com menos de 5 quilos podem ter representado uma importante fonte nutricional para os primeiros hominínios.

Segundo os pesquisadores, presas menores são menos custosas e mais fáceis de capturar, e sua exploração pode ter funcionado como uma etapa anterior ao surgimento da caça de animais maiores . O estudo, porém, não afirma que os macacos-prego reproduzam diretamente o comportamento de nossos ancestrais.

Para os autores, o hábito observado nesses primatas oferece um modelo para investigar os fatores que favorecem a exploração de pequenos animais e refletir sobre o possível papel desse recurso na evolução humana.

Ao final do trabalho, os pesquisadores sugerem que conjuntos arqueológicos antigos contendo restos de pequenos vertebrados sejam reavaliados em busca de sinais de predação. A hipótese é que essas presas possam ajudar a compreender melhor as etapas que antecederam a exploração sistemática de grandes animais pelos humanos.

Uma mulher de 41 anos foi morta a tiros após ter uma discussão com companheiro, de 32, em Salto (SP), na madrugada deste sábado (5). O homem foi preso.

Conforme a Guarda Civil Municipal (GCM) uma equipe foi acionada para atender uma ocorrência envolvendo a briga de um casal na Avenida Eugênio Coltro, no bairro Salto Ville, mas ao chegar no endereço, encontrou a mulher morta. Ela levou quatro tiros.

O companheiro de Maria das Graças Mouzinho da Rocha foi apontado como principal suspeito do crime e foi localizado durante a fuga, na Avenida Roque Lazzazzera. Ele confessou ter matado a mulher e indicou o local em que havia deixado a arma do crime.

Uma pistola 380 foi localizada e apreendida. O homem foi preso em flagrante e vai responder por homicídio.

articles.title: Mãe mantém esperança após oito meses do desaparecimento de crianças | G1
articles.standfirst: Ágatha Isabelly e Allan Michael desapareceram após saírem para brincar na zona rural de Bacabal. A investigação segue sob segredo de Justiça.
articles.summary: Ágatha Isabelly e Allan Michael desapareceram após saírem para brincar na zona rural de Bacabal. A investigação segue sob segredo de Justiça.
articles.body:
O desaparecimento dos irmãos Ágatha Isabelly, de 6 anos , e Allan Michael, de 4 , completou oito meses na sexta-feira (4), sem informações sobre o paradeiro das crianças. Eles desapareceram em 4 de janeiro de 2026 , na comunidade quilombola São Sebastião dos Pretos, na zona rural de Bacabal , a 250 km de São Luís .

Para a mãe, Clarice Cardoso, a vida parou desde o dia em que os filhos desapareceram. Apesar da falta de respostas, ela afirma que mantém a esperança de reencontrá-los.

“Mãe nenhuma desiste de filho, né? E eu não vou desistir dos meus filhos. Eu nunca vou perder minha esperança de encontrar os meus filhos vivos. Eu sonho e tenho fé que esse dia vai chegar”, disse.

Ao longo dos últimos oito meses, o caso mobilizou forças de segurança, voluntários e representantes do Congresso Nacional. No entanto, nenhuma pista concreta sobre o paradeiro das crianças foi divulgada até o momento .

A última visita de representantes do Congresso Nacional à comunidade ocorreu em maio . O grupo fazia parte da Comissão Externa sobre Prevenção e Enfrentamento à Violência Sexual Infanto-Juvenil, criada semanas antes.

Com autorização para realizar diligências, vistorias técnicas e acompanhar denúncias graves no país, os parlamentares vieram ao Maranhão para ouvir a mãe das crianças e autoridades responsáveis pela investigação.

Crianças desaparecidas no Maranhão: veja cronologia do caso

Os avós maternos, que moram ao lado da casa de Clarice, também tentam enfrentar a saudade com a esperança de que os netos estejam vivos.

“A esperança nunca acaba, porque se tivesse acontecido alguma coisa, a gente já tinha uma resposta. A esperança sempre é de encontrar. ”, disse José Emídio Prego Reis, avô das crianças.

A avó Francisca Cardoso acredita que os netos podem ter sido levados por alguém. Segundo ela, o barulho de helicópteros ainda provoca lembranças das operações realizadas na comunidade.

“A esperança para mim nunca morreu. A gente chora, tem dia que a gente dorme bem, tem dia que a gente não dorme, é assim. Na minha mente eles foram levados. Alguém está com eles, escondido. E bem escondido, porque você não acha nada, ninguém não vê, ninguém não comunica nada”, disse.

Menino de 8 anos foi encontrado na tarde desta quarta-feira (7), na zona rural de Bacabal. — Foto: Reprodução/TV Mirante

Ágatha e Allan desapareceram após saírem para brincar com o primo Anderson Kauã, de 8 anos , que é autista. O menino foi encontrado com vida por moradores três dias depois , a cerca de quatro quilômetros do local onde as crianças desapareceram.

Segundo o pai, apesar do acompanhamento psicológico, Anderson ainda não consegue explicar o que aconteceu após o grupo entrar na mata.

Após receber alta médica, Anderson participou da reconstituição do caminho percorrido pelas três crianças , com autorização da Justiça. Segundo o relato do menino, o grupo saiu para procurar um pé de maracujá e entrou por outro caminho na mata para não ser visto por um tio.

Anderson também indicou uma cabana abandonada, conhecida como “ casa caída ”, próxima ao Rio Mearim, onde as crianças teriam passado.

Buscas mobilizaram cerca de 2 mil pessoas

Comunidade mobilizada: centenas ajudam nas buscas por crianças desaparecidas em Bacabal (MA) — Foto: Reprodução/ TV Mirante

O desaparecimento mobilizou policiais civis e militares, bombeiros, integrantes das Forças Armadas e voluntários . Ao todo, cerca de 2 mil pessoas participaram das buscas por terra e água .

As equipes utilizaram helicópteros, drones, cães farejadores, mergulhadores e equipamentos de sonar. As varreduras passaram por áreas de mata fechada, rios, lagos e pelas margens do Rio Mearim, mas nenhum vestígio das crianças foi encontrado.

Objetos e roupas também chegaram a ser localizados durante as operações . A família e a Secretaria de Estado da Segurança Pública do Maranhão informaram, porém, que os materiais não pertenciam às crianças .

As buscas em campo foram reduzidas após as equipes percorrerem a área delimitada pela investigação. A apuração passou a se concentrar no trabalho investigativo .

Em nota, a Secretaria de Estado da Segurança Pública do Maranhão (SSP-MA) informou que os trabalhos para localizar Ágatha e Allan continuam. O órgão afirmou que não pode divulgar detalhes porque a investigação está sob segredo de Justiça.

A secretaria também reforçou que informações que possam ajudar a localizar as crianças podem ser repassadas pelo telefone 190 , da Polícia Militar, ou pelo 181 , do Disque-Denúncia. Não é necessário se identificar.

Nos últimos meses, publicações falsas nas redes sociais afirmaram que as crianças teriam sido encontradas ou que seriam vítimas de uma rede internacional de tráfico de órgãos. Também circularam relatos falsos sobre confrontos e mortes de agentes públicos.

A Secretaria de Segurança Pública afirmou que conteúdos falsos ou sem confirmação podem prejudicar a investigação e ampliar o sofrimento da família.

articles.title: Motoristas encaram filas rumo ao litoral de SP na véspera do feriado | G1
articles.standfirst: O tempo chuvoso não afastou os turistas da Baixada Santista no fim de semana que antecede o feriado da Independência do Brasil.
articles.summary: O tempo chuvoso não afastou os turistas da Baixada Santista no fim de semana que antecede o feriado da Independência do Brasil.
articles.body:
Motoristas encaram filas na Rodovia dos Imigrantes rumo ao litoral paulista — Foto: Ecovias/Divulgação

Os motoristas com destino ao litoral de São Paulo enfrentam congestionamento nas rodovias do Sistema Anchieta-Imigrantes (SAI) na manhã deste sábado (5), que antecede o feriado da Independência do Brasil.

O tempo chuvoso não afastou os turistas da Baixada Santista. A expectativa da Ecovias, concessionária que administra o SAI, é que até 330 mil veículos passem pelas rodovias até o feriado de segunda-feira (7).

A Ecovias informou, por volta das 12h , que os motoristas que descem a serra em direção ao litoral paulista encaram lentidão nas duas rodovias: Anchieta e Imigrantes. Além do excesso de veículos, há neblina nas vias.

📍Rodovia dos Imigrantes Do km 40 ao km 43

📍Interligação Planalto Interdição nos dois sentidos devido à neblina

As quatro principais rodovias que ligam ou passam pela Baixada Santista têm estimativas que somam 1,29 milhão de veículos durante o feriado prolongado da Independência, entre sexta-feira (4) e terça-feira (8).

A previsão considera o Sistema Anchieta-Imigrantes (SAI), a Mogi-Bertioga (SP-098) e os trechos Norte e Sul da SP-055. Os números foram divulgados pela Ecovias Imigrantes e pela Concessionária Novo Litoral (CNL).

A soma das estimativas não representa, necessariamente, 1,29 milhão de veículos diferentes. Isso porque um mesmo veículo pode passar por mais de uma das rodovias contabilizadas pelas concessionárias durante o deslocamento.

articles.title: São Paulo tem chuva e ventos; céu nublado faz 'dia virar noite' | G1
articles.standfirst: Frente fria provoca mudança no tempo na capital neste sábado (5). Defesa Civil alerta para chuva forte, alagamentos e queda de árvores.
articles.summary: Frente fria provoca mudança no tempo na capital. Defesa Civil alerta para chuva forte, alagamentos e queda de árvores.
articles.body:
Céu nublado deixou a Zona Sul de São Paulo, perto da Ponte Estaiada, com o 'dia virando noite'. — Foto: Kleber Tomaz/g1 SP

A cidade de São Paulo teve uma manhã de chuva, ventos fortes e céu nublado neste sábado (5). Em diferentes pontos da capital, a mudança nas condições do tempo deixou o céu com aspecto de noite mesmo durante o dia (veja fotos nesta reportagem) .

A chuva começou a atingir a cidade desde as primeiras horas da manhã. Segundo o Centro de Gerenciamento de Emergências Climáticas (CGE) da Prefeitura, o sábado começou com muita nebulosidade e chuvas passageiras. A temperatura chegou a ficar em torno de 15,9°C durante a madrugada.

A previsão é de que as instabilidades ganhem força ao longo do dia com o avanço de uma frente fria pelo litoral paulista. São esperadas pancadas de chuva de moderada a forte intensidade, raios e rajadas de vento que podem superar os 40 km/h.

Alguns apartamentos estavam com as luzes acesas perto das 11h de sábado (5) devido à escuridão — Foto: Kleber Tomaz/g1 SP

A Defesa Civil do Estado emitiu alerta para chuva forte neste sábado . Há possibilidade de elevados acumulados de chuva, com risco de alagamentos, inundações e deslizamentos, especialmente na Região Metropolitana de São Paulo.

O Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet) também mantém alerta amarelo, de perigo potencial, para tempestades em todo o estado de São Paulo.

Na capital, a temperatura máxima prevista é de cerca de 22°C. O tempo deve continuar instável durante o fim de semana, com queda mais acentuada das temperaturas nos próximos dias.

As imagens registradas na manhã deste sábado mostram o céu carregado e a mudança brusca nas condições do tempo em São Paulo. A recomendação dos órgãos de meteorologia e da Defesa Civil é que a população fique atenta a novos alertas durante a passagem da frente fria.

O Cais da Estação de Santa Luzia está temporariamente interditado para obras de manutenção em Angra dos Reis (RJ). A iniciativa é uma medida preventiva para garantir a segurança dos usuários e a regularidade das operações.

articles.title: A 3-year-old Iowa girl started a library challenge in January; 8 months later she had read 1,000 books before kindergarten
articles.summary: US News: In January, a 3-year-old girl in Iowa signed up for a local library challenge with a simple goal: read as many books as possible before starting kinde.
articles.body: In January, a 3-year-old girl in Iowa signed up for a local library challenge with a simple goal: read as many books as possible before starting kindergarten. By early September, just eight months later, she had reached a milestone that many adults would find daunting: 1,000 books. Her name is Rosie Bentley, and her accomplishment has drawn attention from neighbours, librarians and local media as an inspiring example of early literacy and family support. As reported by the Sun Courier, Rosie’s journey from a toddler with a stack of picture books to a 1,000-book reader shows how small, daily habits can add up to something extraordinary before a child even steps into a school classroom. Read on to know more:A challenge built for little readersThe program Rosie joined is part of a nationwide effort known as 1,000 Books Before Kindergarten. Libraries across the United States offer the challenge to encourage families to read regularly with young children. The idea is straightforward. If a child reads one book a day, they will reach 1,000 books in about three years. Many children start the challenge as infants or toddlers and work toward the goal over several years.Rosie began the challenge at age 3, giving her less time than most participants. She started in January with the expectation that she would work toward the milestone over a longer period. Instead, she moved through books at a pace that surprised even her librarians. By the time she was ready to start kindergarten in the fall, she had already logged her 1,000th book.How a toddler reads 1,000 booksReading 1,000 books does not mean sitting down for 1,000 long story sessions. For a 3-year-old, most of those books are short picture books, board books and early readers that can be finished in a few minutes. Many children hear the same books multiple times, and each reading counts toward the challenge. Repetition is a key part of early literacy. It helps children recognise words, understand story structure and build confidence.Rosie’s routine likely included multiple books per day. A few books at breakfast, several more before nap time and a handful as part of the bedtime routine can quickly add up. On some days, she may have heard 10, 15 or more books. On lighter days, she may have read just a few. Over eight months, those daily sessions accumulated into a four-digit total.The role of family and routineBehind every young reader who reaches a big milestone is a family that makes reading a priority. Rosie’s parents and caregivers helped by having books at home and taking them along when they went out. They also made time to read every day, even when their days were jam-packed. Going to the library regularly, checking out new titles, and attending story times also helped. And to keep her motivated, they monitored her progress and may have given her small rewards on completing little milestones of the challenge.“The library is the best!”, Rosie told RPL Director Michelle Sieh after completing her reading challenge, according to the Sun Courier.Importance of early readingResearch consistently shows that children who read early on have better language skills, larger vocabularies and are better prepared to learn to read independently.Stories teach children how books work, such as turning pages and following a story from beginning to end. It also creates a positive association with reading, making it feel like a comforting ritual rather than a chore.For Rosie, hitting the 1,000-book mark before she’s even started kindergarten means she’s already spent hundreds of hours listening to stories, looking at pictures and talking about characters and plots with her family. She will build on those experiences in the years ahead at school. Teachers often report that children who have had many rich read‑aloud experiences are better able to adjust to classroom routines and are more likely to show interest in books and literacy activities.With a thousand books under her belt, Rosie is stepping into kindergarten with a massive head start. Those eight months of non-stop reading built habits that will pay off for years, whether she’s tackling summer library challenges or picking up her first chapter books. Her family might set a new goal or simply let her follow her curiosity, but the main thing is keeping story time a relaxed, daily habit.How to raise a readerFor other parents hoping to build that same passion, you don't need a rigid strategy or a massive budget:Start early: Babies absorb language long before they can follow a plot.Anchor it to daily routines: Bedtime, breakfast, or quiet time right after school work best.Lean on your local library: It gives you endless variety without filling your house with clutter.Let kids lead: If they want to read the exact same book ten nights in a row, roll with it.In the end, it was never about hitting a magical number. The real goal is creating a comfortable routine, sharing quiet moments together, and helping a child fall in love with a good story.A community celebration of the readingThe local library celebrates Rosie’s 1000th book completion with a party. The librarians congratulated her and gave her a certificate or some sort of special recognition that was tied to the program, as per report. Local news features and library social media posts might show photos of Rose with her favourite books or standing in front of library shelves.These moments count. They send a message to other families that reading matters and that even very young children can accomplish big things. Seeing a fellow student get accolades for reading is a huge motivation for Rosie’s classmates. It makes the idea of 1,000 books feel real instead of abstract.A small girl with a big head startAt 3 years old, Rosie has already accomplished something that many adults admire. With the support of a child, access to books and a regular routine, she has demonstrated that age is no barrier to setting and achieving ambitious goals. Her 1,000-book trip reminds us that early literacy is built one story at a time, often in the quiet moments on a couch or at the kitchen table.Rosie leaves the library with more than a certificate as kindergarten approaches. She carries a lifetime of positive associations with books, a family that values reading and a head start that will serve her well in school and beyond. In her community, she has become a small but powerful example of what is possible when a young child, a caring family and a local library work together.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Output overdrive: 30% productivity boost could power 35% of future manufacturing
articles.summary: India News: India's manufacturing sector could get nearly 35 per cent of its future output simply by getting its workforce 30 per cent more productive.The finding.
articles.body: India's manufacturing sector could get nearly 35 per cent of its future output simply by getting its workforce 30 per cent more productive.The finding comes from KPMG's analysis of more than 130 large Indian manufacturing companies over 10 years. It found that companies which improved productivity faster than their peers also saw stronger growth in profits and market value.Their net profits grew by around 10-11 per cent annually, compared with about 7 per cent for companies with average productivity.The difference was even wider in market value. Companies leading in productivity recorded around 19 per cent CAGR in market capitalisation, against nearly 10 per cent for average-productivity organisations.Overall, productivity-leading companies saw more than 50 per cent higher profitability growth and twice the market-cap expansion compared with their peers.Small factories lag larger firmsThe gains, however, are not spread evenly across the manufacturing sector.More than 70 per cent of large manufacturing companies would need transformative measures to achieve the productivity growth rate required for India's manufacturing ambition, the report said.There is also a wide gap between smaller and larger factories. Small and unorganised manufacturing facilities produce less than 20 per cent of the output per worker compared with large firms.Even among companies within the manufacturing sector, productivity can vary sharply, with differences ranging between 300 per cent and 1,000 per cent.Six ways to drive manufacturing growthKPMG identified six broad levers for manufacturing growth:ProductivityWorkforce shiftsGlobal integrationInvestment in capacityInnovation and technologyConsumption-led growth.But productivity stands out because its benefits can continue over time.“Productivity is Indian manufacturing's most powerful growth lever,” the report said, adding that productivity gains “embed permanently into the system, raising output, margins, and competitiveness year after year.”“Unlike scale or demand-led levers, productivity improvements embed permanently into the system,” the report said.The report said improving productivity would require companies to rethink how work is organised, how organisations are structured and how their workforce is deployed.Digital and AI tools, performance management and changes in workplace culture would also be needed to support these changes, it said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Trump envoys arrive in Moscow ahead of Ukraine talks
articles.summary: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are due to hold talks with Russia before travelling to Ukraine on Sunday.
articles.body:
Two of US President Donald Trump's top envoys have arrived in Moscow ahead of a weekend of talks aimed at accelerating efforts to end the war in Ukraine.

Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will hold talks in the Russian capital before travelling to Kyiv on Sunday for discussions with Ukraine.

Trump told reporters on Friday that Witkoff and Kushner were "bringing with them a proposal to end the war". So far, efforts from the US and its allies to broker a peace deal have failed to deliver a breakthrough.

Both Russia and Ukraine have said they will halt strikes on each others' capital cities for three days while the delegation conducts its visit.

Zelensky said on Saturday that he had spoken to the envoys, who have "already begun working with the Russian side today".

"The plan for tomorrow's diplomatic engagements in Kyiv, involving the US team, has been approved. We are waiting for Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and are ready for a substantive conversation," he added.

"From now through the end of Saturday, as well as on Sunday and Monday, Ukraine is ready to refrain from strikes on Moscow, and we expect the Russians to do the same regarding Kyiv."

Russian state media reported that President Vladimir Putin had ordered a halt to strikes on Kyiv for three days due to the US visit.

Witkoff and Kushner were pictured being greeted by Russian diplomat Kirill Dmitriev after landing at Moscow's Vnukovo Airport.

Flight tracking data showed a US government plane had travelled from Helsinki, Finland, where it flown to from the US earlier in the day.

US news outlet Axios reported that the US envoys would separately meet both Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.

Kushner and Witkoff have visited Russia several times but the talks on Sunday would be the first in Ukraine.

Delegations from Ukraine have attended talks in the US over the past 18 months.

Earlier on Saturday, Zelensky said Russia had fired "demonstrative" strikes on airports in Kyiv and Boryspil overnight ahead of his planned meeting with the US.

Ukraine's president added: "Clearly, these Russian strikes on the airports are a reaction to the discussions and preparations for the possibility of the US side using an aircraft to travel to Ukraine and land at Kyiv Airport or Boryspil Airport."

Ukraine's airspace has been closed since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022.

Zelensky said on Friday he would guarantee the safety of Russian airspace during the envoys' visit and called for Russia to do the same for Ukraine.

He also said an overnight Russian strike on a civilian building in the Dnipro region killed four people and injured five others.

Witkoff and Kushner's visit to Moscow comes just over a week after a rare visit to the Russian capital by the head of the CIA, John Ratcliffe.

There was no official comment from Washington or the Kremlin on what was discussed. Speaking last week, Trump described the meeting as "semi-routine".

Last year, the US, Ukraine and Russia separately suggested that a deal to end the war was edging closer following a flurry of talks brokered by the Americans.

European allies also held talks in Paris but discussions ultimately ended without a breakthrough. Key disagreements remain between the warring sides on issues such as territory and security guarantees for Ukraine.

In recent months, both Russia and Ukraine have intensified their aerial attacks as fighting continues.

Ukraine said it has struggled to repel attacks due to a lack of interceptor missiles, while Kyiv has focused its strikes on Russian economic infrastructure targets.

articles.title: Father who rejected Democrats' sympathy rips 'ignorance' after emotional Capitol Hill hearing
articles.summary: Marcus Coleman rejected Democratic lawmakers' sympathy at a Capitol Hill hearing, saying none ever reached out after his daughter's life-changing crash.
articles.body: A father rejected Democratic lawmakers' expressions of sympathy on Capitol Hill this week, accusing them of only showing concern when the cameras are rolling after his daughter was left permanently disabled in a car crash allegedly caused by an illegal immigrant. "I reject your guys' sympathy, to be honest with you. There's no way you guys are sorry," Marcus Coleman told lawmakers Tuesday. Coleman criticized Democratic lawmakers for what he called their "ignorance" during a follow-up interview Thursday, telling Fox News' Trace Gallagher that he struggled to make them understand his position. "Talking with the Democrat representatives, I mean, the language they speak is ignorance, and it's hard for me to translate what I'm trying to say to them," he said. "I can explain it all day, I just can't understand it for them." ANGEL DADS FACE ANOTHER FATHER'S DAY WITHOUT CHILDREN KILLED BY ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS: 'SHE SHOULD BE GRADUATING' His remarks come after a heated CNN discussion about crimes involving illegal immigrants, during which podcast host Leigh McGowan described the discussion as "exhausting." Coleman told Gallagher about his own "exhausting" experience caring for his 7-year-old daughter, Dalilah, after she was critically injured in 2024 when an 18-wheeler traveling at about 60 mph slammed into the car she was riding in. The Department of Homeland Security identified the truck driver as Partap Singh, an illegal immigrant from India who had obtained a commercial driver's license in California. DHS said Singh was driving at an unsafe speed and failed to stop for traffic and a construction zone before the crash. articles.title: Flourishing green communities are changing lives in Devon
articles.summary: Four projects have been nominated in the environmental category in Devon's Make a Difference Awards.
articles.body:
Four projects have been nominated in the environmental category in BBC Radio Devon's Make a Difference Awards.

The Growing Well Garden in Bow, the Sampford Peverell Tree Wardens in mid-Devon, Shallowford Farm on Dartmoor, and Sustainable Hatherleigh are being recognised for making their communities more eco-friendly, wilder and healthier.

They are doing this in a range of ways from planting trees and growing vegetables, to leading bug hunts and rediscovering nature.

The winners of the Make a Difference awards are due to be announced on 24 September at Buckfast Abbey.

Growing Well Garden is part of a green social prescribing project, where gardening is used as a therapeutic tool and helps a doctor connect with her patients in a different way.

Dr Susan Taheri is an NHS GP at Bow Medical Practice and the founder of Growing Well Garden project - she said the scheme reignited her passion for being a GP.

She said meeting patients in a garden can have benefits compared to seeing them a consulting room and describes the garden as her "happy place".

"There's a lot more getting your hands dirty and not worrying too much about germs," she said.

Shallowford Farm in the heart of Dartmoor aims to make rural life accessible.

Retired horticulturalist Charles Staniland's love for the outdoors started in early childhood and he now volunteers there, teaching young people to get their hands dirty.

He said he wanted to show a more physical approach to food, that it doesn't just show up on a plate, and that it's something they can contribute to.

Staniland hopes the project can "encourage a new generation to understand and value the world around them".

"It takes people out of a concrete environment - it's a very good first step into a greener environment," he said.

Sampford Peverell Tree Wardens are an independent, environmentally-focused, volunteer based group which takes care of the parish's greenery.

For Pete Drew and the other wardens, looking after the environment is a community effort, often powered by cake.

The group plants, protects and maintains trees and hedges on publicly owned land, working with councils and landowners.

He said it was about "taking pride in where you live and making local spaces better for everyone".

Sustainable Hatherleigh runs a range of projects to support the community, from leading bug hunts and encouraging wildflowers and biodiversity in the local graveyard to community composting and running a repair café.

Their site in the middle of the town has now been recognised as a county wildlife site.

Jo Pullin and Sustainable Hatherleigh hope to create a resilient future for the area.

Jo Pullin from Sustainable Hatherleigh, Dr Susan Taheri from Growing Well Garden, Charles Staniland from Shallowford Farm and Pete Drew from Sampford Tree Wardens are finalists in the awards.

articles.title: DTC fought conductor for 32 years over Rs 67 fare and his wages, now fined Rs 1 lakh by Delhi HC
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: The Delhi high court has imposed costs of Rs 1 lakh on the Delhi Transport Corporation (DTC) for pursuing a 32-year-old dispute with a bus .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Delhi high court has imposed costs of Rs 1 lakh on the Delhi Transport Corporation (DTC) for pursuing a 32-year-old dispute with a bus conductor over payment of 17 months' back wages, terming the prolonged litigation an abuse of the process of law.According to PTI report, Justice Amit Mahajan dismissed the DTC's challenge to a 2004 Industrial Tribunal order in favour of the conductor, observing that the department's continued litigation over the limited claim had resulted in avoidable expenditure of public money.The court, in its September 2 order, said the DTC could recover the costs from the officer responsible for pursuing what it described as an "insignificant dispute". Of the Rs 1 lakh imposed, Rs 25,000 will be paid to the Delhi High Legal Services Committee, Rs 50,000 to the PM Relief Fund and Rs 25,000 to the conductor.What's the disputeThe dispute dates back to November 1994, when the conductor was accused of failing to issue tickets to three passengers despite collecting a total fare of Rs 67. He was suspended following the incident.Although the enquiry officer had ruled in the conductor's favour, the disciplinary authority disagreed and issued a show-cause notice proposing his removal from service. He was subsequently removed with effect from August 1996.The conductor challenged the action, following which the DTC chairman-cum-managing director set aside his removal. In 1998, the DTC chairman ordered his reinstatement but denied him back wages and reduced his pay scale.The dispute then reached the Industrial Tribunal, which in 2004 held that the punishment was illegal and without basis. It ruled that the conductor was entitled to wages on his regular pay scale, along with arrears arising from the reduced wages and regular wages for the relevant period.The high court stayed the tribunal's order in July 2005, but Justice Mahajan found no legal ground to interfere with the tribunal's findings. The court noted that the DTC had failed to produce the enquiry report or establish a lawful basis for disagreeing with the enquiry officer.Justice Mahajan said the tribunal had taken a "reasonable and plausible view" based on the material before it and that its findings were neither perverse nor legally unsustainable.The court also criticised the DTC for litigating the issue of 17 months' back wages for 32 years, saying the prolonged proceedings over such a limited claim amounted to an abuse of the process of law and caused unnecessary expenditure of public money.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: In the late 1920s, mule deer were brought to Catalina Island; now a judge has ordered for 2,000 of them to be culled
articles.summary: US News: In the late 1920s, mule deer were brought to California's Santa Catalina Island, but years later they have grown into an ecological problem that no on.
articles.body: In the late 1920s, mule deer were brought to California's Santa Catalina Island, but years later they have grown into an ecological problem that no one is able to contain. Twenty-two animals were brought to the island between 1928 and 1933 and by 1947, the population was about 2,500. Originally native to mainland Southern California, the deer had been introduced as game animals and with no established population of large predators on Catalina the introduced herd expanded rapidly, threatening the native plants. Now, according to a report by the New York Post, nearly all of the 2,000 mule deer are set to be killed under a controversial plan designed to save the plants and make the wildfire-prone day-trip destination less combustible.An ecological problemCatalina's native vegetation had evolved under conditions that did not include large populations of browsing deer, and as the herd spread across the island, this distinction mattered. A 2016 study published in Ecology and Evolution reports on one species in particular: Crocanthemum greenei, more commonly known as island rush-rose. The plant is endemic to the Channel Islands and occurs on Catalina. Researchers wanted to determine whether browsing by introduced mule deer was affecting the plant's ability to grow and reproduce. The researchers found that plants that were protected from deer browsing were larger and had greater seed-production success than plants exposed to deer. In the study, heavily browsed plants could fail to produce seeds, while non-browsed plants inside the exclosures produced seeds. That result gave researchers a direct way to connect deer browsing with a specific reproductive problem in an island-endemic plant, while it also showed why population control mattered beyond the number of deer seen across the island.Officials and island managers were considering ways to reduce the population by the late 1940s. One proposal involved capturing the deer and moving them to the mainland, but that effort did not remove the herd: only 150 deer were trapped, and 110 survived capture and transportation, according to historical records summarised by the Catalina Island Conservancy. A hunting season began in 1949, with 477 deer taken that season, and the state had hoped the hunt would remove substantially more animals. The approach continued for decades, but it did not eliminate the population.The deer may be a beloved fixture around Catalina, including in downtown Avalon, but scientists say their appetite for native shrubs has helped invasive grasses take over parts of the island. Those grasses ignite more easily and allow flames to spread faster than the native vegetation they replace, according to Anna L. Jacobsen, a plant biologist at California State University, Bakersfield.Removal over population controlConservation managers were dealing with a different question by 2021: was maintaining a smaller deer herd enough to protect Catalina’s native ecosystem? The Catalina Island Conservancy has used fencing, hunting and other management measures, but deer have continued to browse native vegetation.On Tuesday, a Los Angeles County judge tentatively rejected opponents’ attempt to block the massacre, clearing the way for the Catalina Island Conservancy to begin culling the herd. The nonprofit, which controls 88% of the island, has plans to wipe out most of the deer population over five years. An estimated 200 animals are expected to be hunted with rifles over the next two months.The California Department of Fish and Wildlife approved the conservancy’s plan in January, allowing it to move forward with the killings.Only a small group of deer living near Avalon will be spared and sterilised. Island residents will also be allowed one final hunting season from late October through mid-December. The deer meat will be donated to local tribal groups or used as part of the California condor recovery programs.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Worcestershire Council plea to bin batteries safely after fire
articles.summary: The authority says batteries or battery-powered items should never be put in household waste bins.
articles.body:
A council is urging residents to dispose of batteries and battery-powered items properly, after a large fire at a recycling facility.

Worcestershire County Council said the fire was the "latest warning" of the growing risks posed by batteries entering the waste and recycling system.

It said residents should never place batteries, vapes, power banks or electrical items containing batteries in household bins.

"Products such as vapes, power banks, portable speakers, toys, musical greeting cards and other small electrical items can ignite when crushed, punctured or damaged in household waste," it said.

Councillor Josh Robinson, cabinet member for the environment, added: "This latest fire shows just how quickly things can go wrong when batteries end up in the wrong place."

"These items are small, easy to overlook and often hidden inside everyday products, but the fires they cause are anything but small."

The authority said batteries should be recycled at dedicated collection points at its household waste recycling centres, supermarkets and participating retailers.

articles.title: ‘Stop the boats’: Masked men block roads to Dover port in anti-immigration protest
articles.summary: UK News: Groups of masked men blocked roads leading to Britain’s busiest ferry port in Dover on Saturday in what officials said appeared to be an anti-immigrat.
articles.body: Groups of masked men blocked roads leading to Britain’s busiest ferry port in Dover on Saturday in what officials said appeared to be an anti-immigration protest, disrupting traffic around the major cross-Channel hub.The Port of Dover said all traffic in and out of the port had been stopped because of an “ongoing public order incident” in the town.Kent Police said officers were at the scene and “engaging with protesters”.Videos posted on social media showed several dozen men dressed in black, with their faces covered by scarves and balaclavas, standing across major roads near the port.One video showed demonstrators linking arms across a road while shouting “stop the boats”.Roads blocked, traffic disruptedThe National Highways agency said the protest blocked routes to the port and caused a 4-mile (6.4-kilometre) traffic jam on Saturday morning. The Port of Dover said one road leading to the port had reopened by late morning.Chris Vinson, a Conservative Party local councillor, said the protest appeared to be “illegal migration-related”.“I’m not aware that there’s been any violence, although clearly, having the path of your vehicle blocked by men wearing black paramilitary gear and balaclavas is extremely intimidating,” he said.Kent Police had not immediately provided further details about the nature of the protest.P&O Ferries, which operates services between Dover and Calais in France, said its sailings were going ahead as scheduled. The company said passengers who missed their booked departure would be put on the next available crossing.Dover and the small-boat crossingsDover, around 70 miles (110 kilometres) southeast of London, handled more than 9 million passengers and 2 million freight vehicles in 2025, according to the port’s website.The town has previously seen anti-immigration protests focused on migrants crossing the English Channel from France in small boats.The issue has also become a major political focus in Britain. Reform UK leader Nigel Farage described asylum seekers arriving by small boats as “an invasion” in a speech on Friday.The Labour government says increased law enforcement cooperation between Britain and France has helped reduce the number of people making the Channel crossing this year by more than 40% compared with 2025.Mike Tapp, the Labour MP for Dover, criticised the protesters for disrupting the town.“I bet if you asked any one of those ‘protesters’ they wouldn’t know small boat crossings are down by 40% and we are working hard to fix the mess,” he wrote on social media on Saturday. “Go home, enjoy your weekend/get a job.”The Port of Dover said it remained in contact with Kent Police as the public order incident continued.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Pickleball and dining: Why courts are the new food destinations
articles.summary: The fastest-growing sport in the US is the ‘eatertainment’ trend’s new darling. How long will it last?
articles.body:
Chicago, Illinois — Ask any pickleballer what the kitchen is, and they’ll tell you it’s the 7ft (2.1-metre) nonvolley zone on either side of the net - and why you should stay out of it. But restaurateurs and investors hope the general public will come to associate pickleball with a more literal kitchen - one serving food before, during and after the game.

The pickleball court is no longer only for before lunch or after dinner. In recent years, pickleball "eatertainment" venues have taken off alongside eatertainment venues as a whole, an industry that Rex Reservations estimates at $120bn globally.

What is an eatertainment concept? It’s a venue where patrons come to participate in an activity - bowling, golf simulators, axe throwing, pickleball, darts - while ordering food and drinks. Think TopGolf or Lucky Strike.

Pickleball was the fastest-growing sport in the United States from 2022 to 2025, according to the Sports & Fitness Industry Association, with participation rising by 171.8 percent. Last year, 24.3 million Americans played pickleball, a 22.8 percent increase from 2024. Ease of play, low barrier to entry and the low-impact nature of the sport are frequently cited as reasons for its popularity.

“The smaller court size and lightweight equipment make it accessible across generations and skill levels, so we can play with family and friends who aren’t pickleball regulars,” says regular pickleballer Emily Oprins, 35, of Naperville, Illinois.

And those same reasons are what make pickleball attractive to more casual players who may be intimidated by their local leagues but find an eatertainment venue to be the perfect speed.

articles.title: Sevenoaks Town Council launches campaign to purchase local theatre
articles.summary: But the local authority is having to purchase the freehold from its counterpart council.
articles.body:
A local authority has launched a fundraising campaign to help purchase a theatre.

Sevenoaks Town Council wants to raise £100,000 towards acquiring the Stag Theatre from its higher level counterpart Sevenoaks District Council (SDC).

The town council leases the venue on London Road but has said the building should be transferred to them at no cost.

The district council has instead offered three options - purchase the theatre for £650,000, a 30-year lease at a peppercorn rent or transfer it to SDC's successor authority after local government reorganisation in 2028.

District council leader Kevin Maskell said the options appropriately balanced "supporting local stewardship and protecting public assets".

Tony McEwen, chief executive of the Stag Theatre, told councillors: "It does not feel right to spend public money buying the freehold of a property that is in every meaningful sense already a public asset."

He said the council should buy the theatre "because it gives the town certainty, control and protection for the long term".

Short film celebrates theatre's survival

Councillor Nick Varley said that if the town council makes the purchase it wants the "ability to start an ambitious new future for the Stag".

Another councillor, Claire Shea, said the alternative options came with "more risk".

She said: "We will be launching a fundraising campaign this week to ask residents, theatre-goers, cinema lovers and supporters to help us fill the gap in the finances we need... without increasing council tax."

articles.title: Before McDonald's and Starbucks, Americans packed these once-beloved lunch counters
articles.summary: Luncheonettes gave women a place to eat during the workday and thrived during Prohibition, but America's fast food and car culture have reshaped dining habits.
articles.body: Long before fast-food counters and coffee shops became fixtures of American life, luncheonettes gave generations of Americans an inexpensive place to grab a meal — and helped change where women could eat, work and socialize in public. The casual restaurants serving simple, inexpensive meals, typically at a lunch counter, began emerging in the late 19th century. They boomed during the 1910s and 1920s and remained popular through the mid-20th century. Woolworth's, S.H. Kress, S.S. Kresge, Walgreens and Liggett's were among the best-known names associated with lunch counters and luncheonettes in five-and-dime stores, drugstores and other retail establishments. THE 24-HOUR AMERICAN DINER IS VANISHING — HERE'S WHAT'S DRIVING THE DECLINE Luncheonettes flourished as Americans increasingly moved into cities and paid employment, said Megan Elias, a curator of food and wine history at the Smithsonian's National Museum of American History. "They fit well with a society that was urbanizing and increasingly organized around paid employment rather than family farms," Elias told Fox News Digital. "Luncheonettes offered food that was affordable and predictable with the kinds of starches and fats people often find comforting." Their menus typically featured straightforward fare, including roast meats, soups, sandwiches and regional dishes such as baked beans. But luncheonettes offered more than inexpensive food. WHY RESTAURANT SERVERS CLEAR YOUR PLATE BEFORE EVERYONE FINISHES EATING "Luncheonettes were affordable, and because they were associated with daytime, they had an atmosphere of respectability," Elias said. "Women and children, who were not generally welcomed in saloons or the dining rooms of men's clubs, could feel comfortable in luncheonettes." They also gave women in the workforce a place to eat during the day, New York-based culinary historian Linda Pelaccio told Fox News Digital. Prohibition and World War II further fueled their popularity as soda fountains and luncheonettes became social gathering places and more Americans sought inexpensive meals away from home. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER "They were popular in American society because they were quick and less expensive," Pelaccio said. "You could get a lunch and a cup of coffee … and be on your way." But the same social changes that helped create the luncheonette eventually contributed to its decline. As jobs shifted to suburban office parks, getting lunch increasingly meant driving, helping fuel the rise of fast-food and drive-thru restaurants, Elias said. Americans' tastes also expanded beyond the traditional luncheonette menu. "[The luncheonette's decline] is a story of the diversification of the American diet, of increased comfort with foods from many different cultures," Elias said. "It's the story of a shift to car culture rather than walking to lunch." CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS Malls, struggling downtowns, suburban life and a changing workforce further contributed to the luncheonette's disappearance, Andrew P. Haley, associate professor of American cultural history at the University of Southern Mississippi, told Fox News Digital. "A big part was the change in women's roles," Haley said. "In the 1970s, more and more women worked. Sure, they might go to Woolworth's for lunch, but unlike when they were shopping downtown and needed a place to take a break, they now could take a lunch to work — and often choose healthier foods, diet food and less expensive foods." TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Yet for those who remember them, luncheonettes can still evoke something increasingly difficult to find, Elias said, because "sitting shoulder to shoulder with strangers at the lunch counter created a sense of community." Haley is less convinced that people are nostalgic for actual luncheonettes rather than for an idealized version of such establishments. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Nostalgic decor might allow us to imagine for an instant that we are regaining community gathering spaces, but the pre-existing community ties that made those spaces collective is no longer there," Haley said.

articles.title: Putin orders a 72-hour pause in strikes on Kyiv as U.S. envoys visit Russia and Ukraine
articles.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin ordered a 72-hour pause in strikes on Kyiv, the Kremlin said Saturday, as U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Moscow to try to revive a stalled push to end Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
articles.body: Russian President Vladimir Putin ordered a 72-hour pause in strikes on Kyiv, the Kremlin said Saturday, as U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Moscow to try to revive a stalled push to end Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. “Putin has ordered that no strikes be carried out against Kyiv for three days, starting at midnight today,” presidential spokesperson Dmitry Peskov told Russia’s Tass news agency. He said the decision was tied to preparations for Witkoff and Kushner’s planned visit to the Ukrainian capital, which Kyiv has said will take place on Sunday. Peskov also confirmed that Kushner and Witkoff would meet Putin during their visit, but said there was “no talk of new ideas” to end the conflict. The envoys’ trip comes as both sides escalate aerial attacks, more than four years after the Kremlin’s invasion of its neighbor. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Friday that Ukraine would halt airstrikes during the envoys’ visit and urged Moscow to do the same. Washington’s push to end the fighting, now in its fifth year, has lost momentum as U.S. attention has been focused for the last six months on its war with Iran. The envoys were met at the airport by Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev, Russia’s state news agency Tass said. Dmitriev shared photos of him meeting the U.S. delegation as they disembarked, alongside the caption, “Welcome to Moscow Peacemakers.” The last known visit to Moscow by Witkoff and Kushner, U.S. President Donald Trump’s son-in-law, was in January, when they met Putin in the Kremlin. They have never visited Kyiv, but Zelenskyy said he was expecting them in the Ukrainian capital on Sunday. With peace efforts stalled, Russia intensified its attacks on Kyiv and other cities with relentless bombardments recently stretching into daylight hours, taking advantage of Ukraine’s shortage of air defensive systems. On Friday, a Russian drone hit one of the most important government buildings in Kyiv — the headquarters of Ukraine’s Security Service, known as the SBU, which is one of the agencies involved in carrying out deep-strike operations inside Russia. The long-range strikes by Ukraine have hit Russian military facilities, oil refineries and e-commerce hubs, seeking to undermine the Kremlin’s war effort and economy, as well as make ordinary citizens feel the consequences of the war. Zelenskyy links Russian strikes to envoys’ visit The air war between Russia and Ukraine has intensified as troops have struggled to make progress along the 1,250-kilometer (775-mile) front line. Russia has recently been using fast-flying, jet-powered drones, and the recurring wail of air-raid sirens has become part of daily life in Kyiv. In a social media post on Saturday, Zelenskyy said that Russia had carried out overnight strikes on Kyiv and Boryspil international airports, and linked the attack to the planned U.S. visit. “Clearly, these Russian strikes on the airports are a reaction to the discussions and preparations for the possibility of the U.S. side using an aircraft to travel to Ukraine,” he said. “We have taken note of this Russian move, and next week we will adjust our operation accordingly regarding Russian airspace, which has become dangerous because of our drones and missiles in the sky. Of course, there are and will be no threats to diplomacy from our side.” Strikes kill 5 at Ukrainian industrial site Russian attacks killed five people and wounded five more at an industrial facility in Ukraine’s southern Dnipropetrovsk region, local military administration head Oleksandr Hanzha said. He described those killed as employees at the site. “A locksmith, an electrician, a plumber and a machinist. People of peaceful professions. They were simply working their shift. They were doing their job when enemy missiles cut off their lives,” he said. A 62-year-old man was wounded and several homes and an apartment building were damaged in a separate attack on the region’s Nikopol district, Hanzha said. In a statement Saturday, Russia’s Ministry of Defense said it had carried out strikes on two metallurgical plants in the region, describing them as “major suppliers of metal products for Ukraine’s military production.” A further two people were wounded in an overnight Russian attack on Ukraine’s Kyiv region, said Tymur Tkachenko, head of the regional military administration. In the Boryspil district, a fire sparked by a strike partially destroyed a nine-story residential building. Russian forces also repeatedly struck a shopping center in the southern Mykolaiv region with drones overnight, damaging retail premises and sparking fires, Ukraine’s state emergency services said. A 72-year-old man and a 17-year-old girl were hurt. Emergency crews responding to the incident were repeatedly forced to withdraw to safety because of the threat of further strikes, returning whenever conditions allowed, the emergency services said. Russia launched ballistic missiles from its Rostov and Voronezh regions and deployed 167 attack drones overnight, Ukraine’s air force said. The drones included Shahed-type aircraft — around half of them jet-powered — as well as Geran and decoy drones. Ukrainian air defenses shot down or suppressed 128 drones, according to the air force. Elsewhere, Ukrainian attacks wounded three people, including a 14-year-old girl, in Russia’s border region of Belgorod, local officials said. In a statement, Russia’s Ministry of Defense said that its forces had shot down 53 Ukrainian drones overnight.

articles.title: Jaguar Land Rover confirms plans for voluntary job cuts
articles.summary: The firm says it needs to save about £1.7bn over the next two years.
articles.body:
Car manufacturer Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) has confirmed it is opening a voluntary redundancy programme, a year on from a cyber attack which brought production to a halt for more than a month.

The firm said it needed to save about £1.7bn over the next two years as it seeks to adapt to "evolving global market conditions".

It was reported by The Times on Saturday that as many as 4,000 jobs may be lost due to the impact of tariffs and a drop in sales.

The firm told the BBC it had not confirmed the numbers. It said the decision to cut jobs was to help "simplify" the organisation as well as "improve efficiency and build greater resilience".

"Today, we informed our colleagues, and trade union partners that JLR is opening a voluntary redundancy programme offering salaried and management team members the opportunity to leave the business," a spokesperson said.

"We will share further information with our colleagues first."

Unite general secretary. Sharon Graham. said the union had been warning about a "perfect storm" hanging over the automotive industry for some time.

"Death by a thousand cuts has been going on under the nose of successive governments," she said.

She added there had been "intensive" discussions over the weekend about mitigating jobs losses adding that she and Business Secretary, Jonathan Reynolds, would be meeting JLR's chief executive, PB Balaji, next week.

"This is an incredibly worrying and stressful time for JLR workers," said Unite national officer, Des Quinn. "Unite is working round the clock to deliver the best possible outcome."

Meanwhile a government spokesperson said significant action had been taken to support the UK automotive industry by lowering electricity bills for manufacturers as well as financial support for the manufacture and sale of zero emission vehicles.

Reynolds was also understood to have spoken with West Midlands mayor, Richard Parker, about supporting the business and its staff.

JLR said over the past three years, it had strengthened its brands and had prepared for production of its next generation of vehicles.

In July, the company said it expected fewer than 300 people would leave the firm under cost savings plans announced at the time.

The company has its global headquarters at Whitley, Coventry, and manufacturing sites in Solihull and Wolverhampton as well as Halewood on Merseyside.

It employs about 30,000 people in its UK operations, with approximately 10,000 people employed at plants overseas.

The cyber attack in September 2025 led to the shut down of all manufacturing at JLR for several weeks, meaning not a single vehicle rolled off its production lines.

That led to a 27% drop in overall production at the company, which is one of the West Midlands' biggest employers.

The overall cost of the cyber-attack and the subsequent loss of manufacturing was estimated to be £1.9bn.

In June, the firm announced it planned to cut about £1.7bn in costs over the coming years to help towards its recovery from the attack.

JLR had indicated at the time that it would make the savings through cuts in areas such as materials, warranty and fixed costs.
